headline: South Asia: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya.
- Persian Gulf Region: Drone attack on Colombia police base injures civilians, including infant.
- Africa: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
Trump said he wanted to move forward with the controlled blasts but is putting the decision in the hands of the courts.
- Military Times, 9 hours ago: B-2 bomber wings awarded Presidential Unit Citation for Midnight Hammer.
The award marks the first time a bomber unit has been recognized with a President Unit Citation since the Vietnam War.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: Under Hegseth, the OSS rides again — kind of.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth resurrected the OSS, created during the Second World War under "Wild Bill" Donovan.
- Military Times, 7 hours ago: VFW seeks veterans’ input on health care experiences in and out of VA.
Through early January, Veterans of Foreign Wars is conducting a survey of veterans on their health care experiences, including medical treatment received at the Department of Veterans Affairs or in private care.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Robbers reach end of road with rare armoured car heist convictions.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Robbers reach end of road with rare armoured car heist convictions.
A string of robberies targeting armoured money-courier companies has yielded two convictions in two months, but the attacks continue, with the latest incident occurring in Liguanea, St Andrew, earlier this month. The two recent convictions mark the first time in 17 years that individuals have faced sentencing following successful prosecutions for offences linked to armoured-car robberies since the last such conviction in 2009.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Generations bound by Howard.
WESTERN BUREAU: For generations, Howard University has been a home away from home for Jamaicans, where families have sent their children to acquire world-class skills, build successful careers and forge friendships that last a lifetime. From engineers and architects to doctors and lawyers, the historically Black institution in Washington, DC, has helped shape the professional journeys of Jamaicans, with some families establishing traditions that span generations.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians launch airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia: six injured – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Russians launch airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia: six injured – photos.
Six people have been injured in Russian strikes on the city of Zaporizhzhia.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Germany's Merz urges Russia to stop "dangerous provocations" after missiles fall in Poland.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Russia to stop dangerous provocations after Russian missiles fell in Poland, pledging full solidarity with Warsaw.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: "A little miracle": three cats rescued at site of Russian strike in Dymer, one found completely buried – photo.
Rescue workers found a cat under the rubble of a building destroyed in a Russian attack in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast. The animal was completely buried under sand, dust and construction debris but survived. The cat was named Dym and taken to a veterinary clinic.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: NATO strengthens protection after Russian missiles violate Polish airspace.
Poland's Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz says allied aircraft will complement ground-based systems, Polish F-16s and other NATO fighter jets.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Back to 1936? Civil war ghosts haunt Spanish election campaign.
- Politico Europe, just now: Back to 1936? Civil war ghosts haunt Spanish election campaign.
With the far right poised to enter government, politicians are reopening the wounds of a war that began 90 years ago.
- Politico Europe, just now: Peace in Ukraine won’t end Russian sabotage in Europe, Poland warns.
Poland’s intelligence minister says Moscow's hybrid campaign against Europe could persist whether the war goes Russia’s way or not.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Serbia’s Student Movement Criticises European Parliament’s Vukovar Resolution.
Student movement says draft resolution marking 35th anniversary of Croatian town's fall offers only 'one-sided interpretation of the past' and ignores Serb suffering elsewhere during the Croatia war.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Drone attack on Colombia police base injures civilians, including infant.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Drone attack on Colombia police base injures civilians, including infant.
Far-right President De la Espriella steps up offensive as rebel groups strike back with drone strikes, roadside bombs.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: US says Iran is possible culprit in dozens of cyberattacks, bomb threats against ships - report.
As many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemical products and other explosive substances are believed to have been attacked, the WSJ said, citing US officials.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Qatar PM looks to revive US-Iran talks after meeting Rubio.
Qatar’s Prime Minister says he’s working towards deescalating tensions between Iran and the US.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Iran hits US bases and civilian sites in the Gulf after a lull.
Tehran has ramped up attacks in recent days as the US naval blockade and sanctions campaign hurt the country.
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 17 hours ago: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The United Nations and the United States have condemned Sunday's drone attacks in Sudan's capital, Khartoum, which damaged a civilian neighborhood and UN premises, as Sudan renewed allegations that drones used in attacks across its territory were launched from Ethiopia.
- Africanews, 14 hours ago: Libyan naval forces remain on high alert after strike on Russian vessel in Benghazi.
A military official says that naval forces in eastern Libya will remain on high alert to counter any threat after attacks targeted two vessels, including at least one Russian ship, off Benghazi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that Ukrainian forces were behind the strikes.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Drone strikes hit homes and UN premises in Sudan's capital.
The United Nations confirmed that one of its premises, with UN personnel inside, was damaged in the attacks. It condemned the risks posed to humanitarian workers in civilian areas.
- Africanews, 19 hours ago: UN calls for probe after drone attacks hit ships off Libya.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for either strike on Sunday off the port city of Benghazi, but they came as Ukrainian forces stepped up attacks against Russia far from the front lines.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Is South Africa Losing Ground Against HIV? These Four Graphs Offer a Warning.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 17 hours ago: South Africa: Is South Africa Losing Ground Against HIV? These Four Graphs Offer a Warning.
[Bhekisisa] Findings from one of the world's largest ongoing population surveys tracking HIV, in rural KwaZulu-Natal, are "a sobering warning", researchers say. All four indicators they analysed show that the momentum in bringing the HIV epidemic under control has been lost -- which could mean it could start growing again. It's a pivotal moment, experts say. South Africa will have to get smart about testing people and getting them on to treatment or prevention if the country were to end HIV as a public health

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, AllAfrica - Conflict, Ukrainska Pravda, Times of India - Top Stories, The Moscow Times, 8 hours ago: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya.
President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines. But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”. “It all took place off the coast of Libya.
- The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: 17 killed in Saudi attack on Yemeni city: Houthis.
Coalition airstrikes on telecoms facilities killed 17 workers, wounded 11 more, and caused the “total destruction” of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other sites, the Houthis’ Telecommunications Ministry said
- The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran.
War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: Bangladesh vows to arrest Hasina if she returns from India.
Bangladesh will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, a senior government minister said, as her plans to come home in December fuel political tension and renewed street violence. Dhaka is instead seeking Hasina’s extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024, and expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told Reuters. India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
India - bottom line: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers.
A special NIA court ruled that four men were not guilty of aiding terrorists in the 2020 attack. The prosecution could not establish any direct link between the men and the terrorists involved in the incident. Although two Army soldiers were killed, the evidence presented was circumstantial and insufficient. The court emphasized the necessity of legal proof despite the crime's severity and implications.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: US probes Iran, Russia link after 50 vessels face cyberattack: Report.
Washington is investigating Iran's potential involvement in numerous cyberattacks against energy tankers carrying hazardous materials. This probe includes incidents where vessels received bomb threats alleging possible explosions. The investigation comes amid concerns that the conflict may expand beyond the Middle East into cyber operations. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: ‘Severe explosions, fires’: Iran claims 3 oil tankers struck mines in Hormuz.
Three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours. Iranian military officials claimed these vessels were escorted by the US Navy while navigating the passage. According to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, US military support could not prevent these incidents from occurring. The IRGC warned vessel owners against ignoring maritime warnings and unauthorized routes through the region.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Pakistan set to invite India to a series of SCO events, but will Delhi join in?.
In an unexpected diplomatic turn, Pakistan is set to invite India for a culture ministers meeting next year, marking a notable engagement since the Pahalgam terrorist attack. Following this, Pakistan will also host the SCO heads of state council summit in August. Although PM Narendra Modi's attendance is unlikely, a senior minister may attend, contingent on the prevailing security environment that will heavily influence India’s diplomatic decisions.
Asia - bottom line: Israel leadership rivals clash over Iran threat ahead of coalition talks.
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Israel leadership rivals clash over Iran threat ahead of coalition talks.
Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, said he saw no immediate reason for attacking Iran on Monday, contradicting caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who warned against playing down “grave threats”. The remarks from both politicians came hours before their parties were due to meet for the third time to discuss possible coalition-building, after lengthy negotiations the day before delivered no breakthrough. - South China Morning Post - China, just now: Malaysia’s Anwar says Beijing ‘extremely reasonable’ in South China Sea talks.
China has been “extremely reasonable” in its negotiations with Malaysia over their competing claims in the South China Sea and discussions will continue as long as certain core sensitivities are respected, according to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. - Taipei Times, 3 hours ago: Finnish parliament warms to hardening border with Russia.
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: EU proposes banning Russian flags at sports events under new sanctions.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has announced a proposal for the next sanctions package over Russia’s war against Ukraine that would ban Russian teams and individual athletes from competing under the Russian flag at events in the EU in the future. The plan also includes banning the display of official Russian symbols and restricting financial flows from Russian sponsors to sports and cultural associations based in Europe. Russian nationals would also no longer be allowed to...

- NK News, 19 hours ago: US senator warns North Korea growing ‘more lethal’ due to Ukraine war.
North Korea’s deployment of troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine is turning the country into a more capable military threat, a prominent U.S. senator has warned, arguing that this will constrain Washington’s freedom to act. Australia - bottom line: Israel's bombardment has turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland'.
- ABC News Australia, 4 hours ago: Israel's bombardment has turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland'.
New research suggests more than 99 per cent of the Gaza Strip shows signs of contamination from Israeli attacks.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Iran-based operation used ChatGPT to create fake news, influence Australians.
An Iran-based foreign influence operation used AI to create a fake journalist that wrote news articles and posts on X about Australia's involvement in the US-Iran war, the ABC can reveal.
- ABC News Australia, 5 hours ago: Staff at regional hospital warn of mass exodus over reduced doctor roster.
Whistleblowers tell the ABC a reduction in rostered doctors in WA reflects health authorities' reliance on telehealth in country emergency departments.
